title: Late Charge Base on Operating Lines of Credit Bills Whose AutoDraft Debit Came Back Unpaid
content:
When an Operating Lines of Credit interest bill was debited by AutoDraft and the debit came back unpaid, the reason for the return decides the charge base of any late charge on that bill.

## Rule

The charge base is:

- **the bill's full billed amount, whatever was paid on it afterwards**, when the bill's AutoDraft debit came back unpaid for a reason other than unauthorized;
- **the billed amount less every payment applied to it, the returned debit counted as paid**, when that debit came back unpaid as unauthorized;
- **the billed amount less the payments applied to it**, when no AutoDraft debit of the bill came back unpaid.

The bill's AutoDraft debit is the latest interest payment on that bill collected by AutoDraft; whether it came back unpaid, and the return reason, are shown by the returned payment entry pointing to that debit in the line's transaction history.

## Cases (hypothetical bill of USD 4,000.00: an AutoDraft debit of USD 2,000.00 and a later phone payment of USD 500.00 applied to it)

| What happened to the AutoDraft debit | Charge base |
|---|---|
| Returned unpaid, reason other than unauthorized | USD 4,000.00 — the full billed amount |
| Returned unpaid as unauthorized | USD 4,000.00 less USD 2,000.00 and USD 500.00, that is USD 1,500.00 |
| Not returned | USD 4,000.00 less USD 2,000.00 and USD 500.00, that is USD 1,500.00 |

## Question on the rule

**A debit came back unpaid for a reason other than unauthorized and the member then paid part of the bill by phone. Does that payment lower the charge base?** No. In that case the charge base is the bill's full billed amount, whatever was paid on it afterwards.
